description: Political actors frame fertility migration aging youth or diversity as existential threat.
Repeated climate disasters and slow-onset stress increase internal displacement urban absorption pressure and cross-border movement.
States respond to mobility pressure through deterrence externalization irregularity and exclusion.
Aging societies rely heavily on migrant care workers without adequate rights or wage protections.
Large youth cohorts face weak education unemployment housing barriers and limited political voice.
Older population shares rise while care systems pensions housing and health systems remain underprepared.
Legal pathways labor protections integration asylum capacity and local support improve mobility governance.
Cities invest in housing transit schools health public space and integration as populations change.
